items.headline: U.S. Futures Mixed, Oil Prices Climb After Treasury Debt Buyback Announcement
items.summary: U.S. stock futures showed mixed movements this morning, following Wednesday's market close where major indices snapped a three-day losing streak. Investors are reacting to the Treasury Department's plan to significantly increase debt repurchases, which has lowered bond yields, alongside ongoing assessments of hawkish Federal Reserve meeting minutes. Oil prices are rising, suggesting strength in the energy sector.

items.headline: Estée Lauder Surges on Strong Earnings
items.summary: The Estée Lauder Companies Inc. ($EL) saw its stock surge 16.3% following a report of quarterly earnings of $0.39 per share, surpassing the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $0.32, with revenues also exceeding expectations.

items.headline: Toll Brothers Rises on Earnings Beat
items.summary: Toll Brothers, Inc. ($TOL) stock climbed 4% after reporting quarterly earnings of $2.97 per share, exceeding the consensus estimate of $2.90, despite a slight decrease in total revenues year-over-year.

items.headline: Walmart Slides Pre-Market on Cautious Outlook
items.summary: Walmart's stock ($WMT) slid more than 6% in pre-market trading this morning as the retail giant provided a cautious outlook for the year ahead of its quarterly earnings release.

items.headline: Treasury Department Boosts Debt Buybacks, Yields Fall
items.summary: The U.S. Treasury Department announced plans to more than double its repurchases of 10-, 20-, and 30-year government debt over the coming months. This decision contributed to a sharp drop in Treasury yields, with the 10-year yield falling to nearly 4.65% and the 30-year yield to about 5.19%. The move also sparked an 11.5% surge in Bitcoin ($BTC) to $71,808.74 in early trading.

items.headline: Hawkish Fed Minutes and Upcoming Jackson Hole Speech Shape Sentiment
items.summary: Investors continue to digest the minutes from the Federal Reserve's latest meeting, which indicated a potential for further interest rate hikes. Attention is now shifting to Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's upcoming speech at Jackson Hole next week for further policy guidance.

items.headline: U.S. Labor Market Shows Unexpected Weakness
items.summary: Recent labor market data delivered a negative surprise, with the unemployment rate rising to 4.5% against a consensus of 4.4%. The economy also saw a loss of 15.8 thousand jobs, contrary to expectations of an 11.7 thousand gain, indicating a slowdown.

items.headline: Oil Prices Climb Amid Geopolitical Tensions
items.summary: Oil prices are on the rise, with Brent crude surging 2.5% to $93.90 a barrel and U.S. benchmark crude jumping 2.8% to $86.72 a barrel. This increase extends gains for the fifth consecutive session, fueled by stalled U.S.-Iran peace talks and ongoing Middle East supply disruptions.

items.headline: Consumer Discretionary, Materials, and Healthcare Led Gains Yesterday
items.summary: On Wednesday, six of the eleven broad S&P 500 sectors closed in positive territory. The Consumer Discretionary Select Sector SPDR (XLY) rose 2.1%, followed by the Materials Select Sector SPDR (XLB) with a 1.7% gain, and the Health Care Select Sector SPDR (XLV) which advanced 3.5%. The Industrials Select Sector SPDR (XLI) was among the lagging sectors, falling 0.9%.

items.headline: Deere & Company Reports Strong Q3 Earnings, Raises Outlook
items.summary: Deere & Company ($DE) reported net income of $1.379 billion, or $5.10 per share, for the third quarter ended August 2, 2026, exceeding expectations. The company also improved its net income guidance for fiscal 2026 to a range of $4.75 billion to $5.00 billion, citing disciplined execution and resilient performance.

items.headline: U.S. National Debt Exceeds $40 Trillion Mark
items.summary: The total U.S. national debt surpassed a record $40 trillion on Wednesday, influenced by soaring defense spending and ongoing U.S. involvement in the Middle East.
